title: openai-responses: add seed/determinism + metadata passthrough and streaming stability fixes
author: Lena Huang
description: Adds support in the OpenAI compatibility layer for newer Responses API variants: explicit seed/determinism flags, and passthrough of user-provided metadata across both streaming and non-streaming response paths. This change also fixes several streaming stability issues (event ordering under backpressure, reconnect/retry semantics for partial streams, and more robust cancellation handling) and improves function/tool-calling compatibility by ensuring metadata and tool-call payloads are translated bidirectionally between Redwood internal proto and OpenAI-style Responses objects. The PATCH keeps existing default behavior (no seed/determinism unless requested) to preserve determinism for current customers, includes comprehensive unit + integration tests against the responses-sim harness, and provides migration notes for SDK consumers. Linear refs: ENG-1082 (Responses API compatibility), ENG-1105 (streaming stability). Related support ticket SUP-342 was used to reproduce a customer streaming metadata loss case. This PR is intended to be backward compatible; a follow-up backport to the last release branch is requested in the labels.
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial translation layer for seed/determinism flags; add metadata passthrough to response proto + event pipeline; streaming event ordering fix (ordered queue + sequence ids); reconnect/retry improvements for partial streams; SDK translations for Python/TS; add integration tests against responses-sim; docs and release notes update.
review_comments: Ethan: Please add a regression test that replays a partial stream then a reconnect; author: added tests in responses_sim/streaming_metadata_test.go and verified sequence ids are preserved; Priya: prefer explicit sequence-id header rather than relying on timestamps; author: switched to explicit sequence header and updated streaming pipeline to enforce ordering; Carlos: minor nit on SDK mapping for function call metadata (should be "tool_id" not "toolName"); author: fixed SDK mapping and added extra test coverage; final approvals after CI green.
ci_checks: CI pipeline: unit tests (pass), integration tests (initially failed on streaming flake, re-run passed), linters (pass), typecheck (pass), e2e responses-sim (pass). One flaky test fixed by ordering change; full run green at 2025-02-12T09:23:00Z.
release_notes:
- OpenAI Responses compatibility: seed and determinism flags supported for reproducible responses and sampling control.
- Metadata passthrough: user metadata provided to generation calls is preserved and surfaced in both streaming events and final Responses objects.
- Streaming stability: fixes for event ordering, reconnect/retry semantics, and cancellation handling under backpressure.
- SDK updates: Python and TypeScript translations for the Responses seed/metadata fields and tool-calling metadata mapping.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-02-12 by automerge-bot. Merge commit: 9f3a7b2 (squash). Backport requested to release-2025-01 branch.
diff_snippet: @@ service/openai_compat/streaming_pipeline.go +12, -8 @@ func handleEvent(e Event) { // ensure sequence ids are enforced and ordering queue used if e.SequenceID > lastSeen { enqueueOrdered(e) } else { emit(e) } }
notes_for_consumers: Default behavior unchanged: seed/determinism are opt-in via the compatibility input. SDKs expose a 'seed' param in openai_compat wrappers; if omitted behavior is identical to previous versions. To opt into deterministic responses provide 'seed' and set 'deterministic: true' where supported. Metadata fields in Responses now contain a 'user_metadata' map that is echoed on streaming events; update any event parsers to read the new key.
testing_summary: Unit tests: +62 coverage on translator and streaming pipeline. Integration: responses-sim reproduced SUP-342 and validated metadata passthrough across reconnects. Manual QA: smoke test with three different OpenAI Responses variants (responses-v1, responses-v1beta, and streaming) across CPU/GPU runners. All tests passing in CI.
